units.name: Drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia
units.assessment: Can you name the drugs most often responsible for drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia, describe the expected interval from exposure to nadir and from withdrawal to recovery, and explain why confirmatory antibody testing rarely helps you in real time?

lesson.note: Re-searched on the culprit drugs rather than the section title — quinine, quinidine, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, vancomycin, linezolid, piperacillin — and on 'drug-dependent platelet antibody'. The second pass returned general ITP material, dengue and HIV thrombocytopenia, coagulation-test tutorials and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Nothing teaches the quinine-type drug-dependent antibody, the exposure-to-nadir and withdrawal-to-recovery intervals, or why confirmatory testing rarely arrives in time to help.
